newsitem.title: USA: Iowa's corn crop thrives, soybeans improve.
newsitem.headline: Iowa's corn crop thrives, soybeans improve.

text.p: Iowa's corn crop was growing faster than farmers could keep up with in the week ended Sunday, according to the Iowa Agricultural Statistics Service weekly report.
"Rapid growth has made it difficult for farmers to cultivate corn between rains and now the crop is past cultivating in most areas," the report said.

The average height of the corn without extending the leaf was 47 inches. One percent was tasseling, behind average of three percent. The crop was rated 84 percent good to excellent, improved from 80 percent last week.

Soybeans were blooming on 13 percent of the acreage, about five days ahead of last year but behind the normal of 14 percent. The crop was rated 76 percent good to excellent, against 71 percent the previous week.
"In general, both crops are doing well in spite of localized damage from wind, hail, ponding and insects," the report said.
Topsoil moisture was rated nil very short, 11 percent short, 82 percent adequate and seven percent surplus.
Pasture conditions were rated one percent very poor, 10 poor, 30 fair, 50 good and nine percent excellent.
